en: Now, what exactly are tree data structures?
Think of data that can be represented like
this.
That would be a tree.
Examples for trees would be
the browser document object model. So in the
end, the HTML code which we write is
organized as a tree. We got one root
element, the HTML element, and then we got a
bunch of child elements which then each can
have more child elements.
And this kind of top-down structure where
one parent can have multiple children and
those children can have more children,
that is a tree.
Another example would be a decision tree.
For example, here, if we're deciding whether
we wanna go for pizza or pasta, depending on
what we choose, we might have more
decisions. So again, that's a tree-like
structure. We get a couple of decisions
where every choice leads to new decisions,
but the decision on whether we wanna pick
meat or veggie depends on whether we chose
pizza or pasta. That is a tree.
So tree structures are everywhere in real
life, but also in programming, and they can
help us work with all kinds of data and
implement all kinds of logic.
Now, if we work with trees, there are
certain terms which we have to know.
For example,
the things, the bubbles here on this slide
are called nodes. So we have a node here,
also called a vertex.
Plural would be vertices.
Now, the connections between multiple nodes
would be edges.
And we also, and that's very important, have
exactly one root node. In a tree,
